Philosophy
 The philosophy of Carrigoran House is to maintain the independence of seniors for as long as possible and to provide them with the dignity they deserve in illness and dying. This is accomplished by providing high quality, comprehensive and person-centred care. 
Our Mission: Why We Exist
 The mission of Carrigoran House is to continue the healing ministry of Jesus Christ in such a way that both givers and receivers of healthcare within our Home experience God's Love and compassion. At every level of this Home, persons work together as a team to provide healthcare as it is shaped by the philosophy, tradition and values of the Sisters of Charity of the Incarnate Word. We commit ourselves to show respect for the human person at every stage of life, especially in sickness, suffering and death, which we see as possible occasions of experiencing God's presence. In these moments, we strive to offer hope, healing and peace. 
Core Values: What we believe in  
Dignity:     Respecting the inherent value and worth of each person.  
Caring Service:     Exceeding customer expectations by providing quality and respectful service.  
Compassion:     Focusing on providing service with a spirit of empathy, love and concern.  
Stewardship:     Cultivating the resources entrusted to us to promote healing and wellbeing.  
Vision
 Carrigoran House will be a leader and advocate in creating excellence in caring services that promote wellbeing of the individual, especially in senior years. Responsible stewardship ensures that Carrigoran House responds in new and innovative ways to deliver quality health care services that promote independence and freedom of choice in a variety of care continuums.

SICK PRIESTS BENEVOLENT FUND COMMITTEE 
                                       CONSTITUTION
The Committee shall be known as the Cloyne Sick Priests Benevolent Fund Committee.
The Committee shall consist of seven members, five of whom are directly elected by the incardinated priests of the Diocese, the outgoing Treasurer being an ex-officio member and the seventh co-opted by the other six.
Membership of the Committee shall be for a period not exceeding five years. Apart from the outgoing treasurer, a member may not serve for more than two consecutive terms.
A Treasurer may not serve a third consecutive term in that office.
The Committee shall advise and assist the Bishop in matters relating to the support of sick and retired priests of the Diocese.
The Committee shall operate under Rules approved by the Bishop after consultation with the Council of Priests.
Any or all members of the Committee may, for a grave reason, be removed by the Bishop, to be replaced according to the Rules.
This Constitution shall be reviewed not later than five years after coming into effect.
CLOYNE SICK PRIESTS BENEVOLENT FUND RULES
1. ELECTION OF MEMBERS
1.1 Towards the end of its term of office, the Committee shall arrange for the election of members of a new Committee and shall appoint two tellers to count the votes.
1.2 All priests incardinated in the Diocese shall be eligible to vote and shall be eligible for election.
1.3 With the exception of the outgoing treasurer, all those who have served two consecutive terms on the committee immediately prior to the election shall not be eligible for election.
1.4 For the purposes of the election, the priests of the diocese shall be divided into five groups, based on date of ordination, with one member to be elected from every group.
1.5 The priest receiving most votes in each group shall be deemed elected. In the event of tie, the issue shall be decided by lot.
1.6 The five elected members shall meet with the out-going treasurer in order to decide on the co-option of the seventh member of the committee.
1.7 The voting returns shall be retained for the purpose of filling a vacancy among the elected members for the remainder of the term of office of the Committee.
1.8 The Committee shall continue to discharge its functions until such time as a new committee has been established, even though its term of office may have expired.
2 OFFICERS
2.1 The Committee shall elect one of its members to act as Chairman at its meetings. In the absence of the Chairman from a particular meeting, the Committee shall elect a member to preside at that meeting.
2.2 The Committee shall elect a Secretary from among its members.
2.3 The committee shall elect a Treasurer from among its members.
3. MEETINGS
3.1 The ordinary meetings of the Committee shall be held as often as the Chairman deems necessary but not less than twice a year.
3.2 The Secretary shall give adequate notice of meetings to all members. 
3.3 The quorum of the Committee shall be four members.
4. CONFIDENTIALITY
4.1 Members of the Committee shall be required to keep confidential all matters discussed at meetings or learned in connection with the work of the Committee unless otherwise agreed by the Committee.
5. POLICY 
5.1 The Committee shall exercise its functions for the care of the sick and retired priests of the Diocese under the provisions of the Policy Document for the Retirement of Priests in the Diocese of Cloyne. This policy shall be determined from time to time by the Bishop after consultation with the committee and with the Council of Priests and the College of Consultors.
6. SEDE VACANTE
6.1 The Committee shall continue to discharge its administrative functions during the vacancy of the See, even though its term of office may have expired until such time as the new Bishop has taken possession of the Diocese.
7. CHANGES IN THE RULES
7.1 These rules may be changed from time to time by the Bishop after consultation with the Committee and with the Council of Priests.

Engaged in schools or in other forms of education, we put our heart and soul into serving the human person for the sake of the Kingdom.
By the tasks they perform, Brothers employed in administration or in manual work cooperate in the apostolate of the Institute. 
Adaptation of our ministry to the needs of the Church and of society calls for discernment and evaluation at regular intervals.
Article 87: The Marist school, as envisaged by Father Champagnat, offers families an approach to education which draws faith, culture, and life into harmony. It is an approach which stresses the values of self-forgetfulness and openness to others, which presents culture as a way of drawing people together, and proposes knowledge as a duty of service.
In our schools, which provides a particularly favourable setting for Christian education, we give priority to a pastoral care that is adapted to the needs of young people. While ready to serve them all, we give special attention to pupils who are in difficulty.
Our schools, which are open to any family that accepts our educational approach, encourage dialogue between persons of different cultures and different beliefs.
Article 88: We share our spirituality and our educational approach with parents, lay teachers, and other members of the educating community. By the service they render, the non-teaching staff collaborate closely in our apostolic task. 
We show our pupils that we are not only their teachers, but also their brothers. By trying to establish in the school a spirit of friendliness and collaboration, we help young people to become responsible for their own formation.
We keep in close contact with former students by friendship and by prayer. We willingly accept their co-operation in the progress of the school. At appropriate times we help them with advice, and encourage them to devote themselves to serving the Church and people.

Our charitable object is the advancement of Religion through the living of a purely Contemplative way of life, as outlined below:
Our Founder St. Dominic instituted the Dominican nuns as an essential part of the Order of Preachers and an efficacious help to the life and apostolate of the brethren. We devote ourselves to praising God and begging unceasingly for the graces necessary for the salvation of all people. This is our primary work (LCM 1).
The Charity supports this charitable work and makes it possible for us to fulfil this obligation entrusted to us by the Catholic Church and the Dominican Order by providing, throughout their lives, for the reasonable needs of the members of the Community who serve as the main object of the Charity (LCM 32, 75, 265, appendix 1:21,22). These duties include:
	To promote the spiritual, moral and intellectual wellbeing of the members (LCM 100).
	To witness to and nurture the Christian faith in both the local and wider Community by providing the opportunity for people to participate in Holy Mass, the Divine Office and Adoration of the Blessed Sacrament, on a daily basis (LCM 1, 83).
	To provide for our Chaplaincy and the upkeep of our Chapel (LCM 88, 265).
	To provide support and comfort to the poor and distressed who seek our prayer, and when desired, to pray with those in need and enrol them in our Association of Prayer whereby they participate in the spiritual benefits of our Contemplative life (LCM 45, 74, 225).
	To promote vocations to our Community and to educate both current and new members of the Community, especially in Sacred Scripture, Theology and Liturgy (LCM 100-102, 111-119).
	To care for our sick and elderly members (LCM 8-13).
	To maintain the property (LCM 265).
	To manage and promote our Retreat house (LCM 83).
	To share our life, and reflections with the public in an effort to turn minds and hearts to God (e.g. through the internet) (LCM 1, 14).
	To aid devotion among the public by writing Icons and producing and selling religious objects, rosary beads, greeting cards and candles (LCM 103-107).
	To provide adequate training, as needed, to ensure the quality and perfection of our work. (LCM 107)
	To assist poorer Monasteries of the Order in so far as our modest means allow (LCM 283).
	To aid, in so far as our resources allow, both our local poor and those in greatest need throughout the world, especially in times of natural disaster and war (LCM 31, 283).
	To support the ministry of our Dominican brothers and sisters through our prayer and penance and at times to provide financial assistance when special projects require aid (LCM 1, 283).

charitable_objects:
CONSTITUTION OF THE
DUBLIN MAR THOMA CHURCH, DUBLIN(Nazareth Mar Thoma Church).
We, the members of the Dublin Mar Thoma Church, Dublin, in its duly convened general body meeting approved the following document as the constitution for the Dublin Mar Thoma Church, Dublin. 
1. Name 
The name of the charity shall be Dublin Mar Thoma Church .
2. Objectives of the charity: 
a.	Main object: The main object for which the body is established is for advancement of the Christian faith, to include worship of the Lord Jesus Christ, to conduct religious sacraments and services in Republic of Ireland especially in greater Dublin area as necessary, in accordance with the faith and practices of The Mar Thoma Church (parent Church), in particular, but not exclusively.
b.	Subsidiary objects:  In furtherance exclusively of the forgoing main object set out above, the group shall have the following subsidiary objects.
i.	To advance the Christian Faith in particular but not exclusively, by engaging in missionary and other charitable Christian activities.
ii.	Provide pastoral care and organize activities to promote the spiritual life of its members; make voluntary contributions for evangelistic and charitable work in Ireland and abroad - especially India.
The Charity may participate in collaborative programmes with other Churches with which it has communal relationships and also participate in all acceptable ecumenical relationships as a full member of the World Council of Churches (WCC), and Churches Together in Britain and Ireland (CTBI).
3. Powers 
a.	In furtherance of the objects but not otherwise the Executive Committee may exercise the following powers:
b.	Power to raise funds and to invite and receive contributions provided that in raising funds the Executive Committee shall not undertake any substantial permanent trading activities and shall conform to any relevant requirements of the law: 
c.	Power to buy, take on lease or in exchange any property necessary for the achievement of the objects and to maintain and equip it for use. 
d.	Power subject to any consents required by law to sell, lease or dispose of all or any part of the property of the Charity. 
e.	Power subject to any consents required by law to borrow money and to charge all or any part of the property of the Charity with repayment of the money so borrowed. 
f.	Power to employ such staff as are necessary for the proper pursuit of the objects and to make all reasonable and necessary provision for the payment of pensions and superannuation for staff and their dependants. With the exception of the Vicar and assistant Vicar, such staff shall not be members of the Executive Committee.
g.	Power to co-operate with other Charities, voluntary bodies and statutory authorities operating in furtherance of the objects or of similar charitable purposes and to exchange information and advice with them. 
h.	Power to establish or support any charitable trusts, associations or institutions formed for all or any one of the objectives.
i.	Power to appoint and constitute such advisory committees, sub committees or commissions as the Executive Committee may   think fit. Conveners of such committees, sub-committees and commissions shall be appointed, from among the members of the Executive committee. All such committees should report to the Executive Committee their actions.
j.	Power to do all such other lawful things as are necessary for the achievement of the objects.
k.	Prescribed items of income, shall be collected and remitted to the Parish treasury, in accordance with existing rules and practices and any modifications made from time to time.
4. Membership & Place of worship
The charity shall have members who believes in the faith, doctrine and practices of the parent church and affirms the same in writing can become a member of the charity in accordance with the constitution of the parent church. The charity will provide all religious services through ordained priests including sacraments like baptism, first communion, wedding, Holy Communion, funeral etc. Presently the charity is worshiping at St Maelruain's Parish, Main Street, Tallaght, Dublin 24. 
5. Registered Agent and Mailing Address
The registered agent of the charity in Ireland is Mr. Sibi Philip and the address of the registered agent is 10, Bramblefield Drive, Clonee, Dublin 15. 
6. Executive Committee Membership and future appointments
The Executive Committee, who are also known as the Charity Trustees, shall consist of not less than ten (10) members and they will hold office until the next annual meeting of the members, which will be held at such times as per the constitution of the parent church. The Executive Committee shall meet at least once in every three months each year. The Executive Committee Membership must partly comprise of the following posts: 
1.	President & Vicar
2.	Vice-President
3.	Secretary
4.	Treasurer
5.	Accountant
6.	Lay Ministrant (2)
7. Determination of Membership of the Executive Committee
A member of the Executive Committee shall cease to hold office if he or she: 
1.	Is not eligible under the constitution of the parent church; 
2.	Becomes incapable by reason of mental disorder, illness or injury of managing and administering his or her own affairs;
3.	Notifies to the Executive Committee a wish to resign in accordance with the constitution of the parent church
8. Income and Property
The income and property of the body shall be applied solely towards the promotion of its main object as set forth in this Constitution.  No portion of the body's income and property shall be paid or transferred directly or indirectly by way of dividend, bonus or otherwise howsoever by way of profit, to the members of the body.  No Officer shall be appointed to any office of the body paid by salary or fees, or receive any remuneration or other benefit in money or money's worth from the body.  However, nothing shall prevent any payment in good faith by the body of:
a)	Reasonable and proper remuneration to any member of the body (not being an Officer) for any services rendered to the body;
b)	Interest at a rate not exceeding 5% per annum on money lent by Officers or other members of the body to the body;
c)	Reasonable and proper rent for premises demised and let by any member of the body (including any Officer) to the body;
d)	Reasonable and proper out-of-pocket expenses incurred by any Officer in connection with their attendance to any matter affecting the body;
e)	Fees, remuneration or other benefit in money or money's worth to any Company of which an Officer may be a member holding not more than one hundredth part of the issued capital of such Company.
9. Keeping of Accounts
Annual audited accounts shall be kept and made available to the Revenue Commissioners on request.
10. Annual General Body Meetings
I.	There shall be an Annual General Body Meeting of the Charity which shall be held before the end of May each year or as soon as practicable thereafter.
II.	Every Annual General Body Meeting shall be called by the Executive Committee. The Secretary shall give notice of the Annual General Body  meeting and the agenda to be considered to all the members of the Charity by announcing during worship service (also by the vicar), on two Sundays, setting out the date and subjects for consideration. In addition the notice may be placed on the notice board and may be sent by post and or given through electronic media.
III.	If twenty percent of the total membership or an aggregate of fifty members, make a written request to the Vicar, to convene a meeting of the General Body, together with the proposed subject for consideration, the Vicar shall convene the Executive committee, as per due procedure, to fix the date and place of the proposed meeting and proceed to convene the General Body Meeting, by due notice. In case, the executive committee fails to take necessary preliminary notice within two weeks. The vicar shall nonetheless proceed to convene the General Body Meeting, within thirty days, from the date of request. If the Vicar fails to convene the General Body Meeting, the matter may be reported to the Diocesan Bishop, and further action shall be taken, as directed by him.
IV.	In emergent circumstances, the Vicar may convene a General Body Meeting, by public announcement, during worship service, on a minimum of one Sunday, so as to be held, after a minimum of three days from the announcement.
V.	Whenever considered necessary, the Diocesan Bishop and the Metropolitan may convene meeting of the General Body by special notice.
VI.	At the General Body Meeting, the vicar shall be the chairman of the meeting, but if he is not present, before any other business is transacted, the persons present shall appoint the vice president or any other person as Chairman of the meeting.
VII.	The Executive Committee shall present to each Annual General Body Meeting the report, annual budget and accounts of the Charity for the preceding year.
11. Winding-up
If upon the winding up or dissolution of the body there remains, after the satisfaction of all its debts and liabilities, any property whatsoever, it shall not be paid to or distributed among the members of the body. Instead, such property shall be given or transferred to some other charitable institution or institutions having main objects similar to the main objects of the body. The institution or institutions to which the property is to be given or transferred shall prohibit the distribution of its or their income and property among its or their members to an extent at least as great as is imposed on the body under or by virtue of Clause 8 hereof. Members of the body shall select the relevant institution or institutions at or before the time of dissolution, and if and so far as effect cannot be given to such provisions, then the property shall be given or transferred to some charitable object.
12. Additions, alterations or amendments
No addition, alteration or amendment shall be made to or in the provisions of this Constitution for the time being in force unless the same shall have been previously approved in writing by the Revenue Commissioners.	
Approved by and signed on behalf of the general body of the charity on 12th of June 2010

9. —A recognised school shall provide education to students which is appropriate to their abilities and needs and, without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing, it shall use its available resources to—

(i) conduct its activities in compliance with any regulations made from time to time by the Minister under section 33 ,

(j) ensure that the needs of personnel involved in management functions and staff development needs generally in the school are identified and provided for,

(k) establish and maintain systems whereby the efficiency and effectiveness of its operations can be assessed, including the quality and effectiveness of teaching in the school and the attainment levels and academic standards of students,

(l) establish or maintain contacts with other schools and at other appropriate levels throughout the community served by the school, and

charitable_objects:
The Congregation of the Sisters of Charity of Jesus and Mary is a religious institute of pontifical right.
As women with a contemplative heart we are committed to living out the gospel values of love, forgiveness, reconciliation and compassion.
At one with the universe and each other we value the whole of creation and journey with all Gods people in faith respecting differences, welcoming diversity and upholding their inherent dignity.
Our communities strive to radiate joy and hope. Aware that every person is unique and precious we are called to empower each other to work for social justice and so be a healing presence in our broken world.
In the spirit of St. Vincent de Paul, the Sisters strive to live according to the exigencies willed for them by their founder; union with God, service of their neighbour and life in community. Their mission of evangelising the poor directs them towards the care of the sick and afflicted, the education of children and young people, and it knows no boundaries. 
Our Founder, Peter Joseph Triest, saw this love (Love of God) as a legacy from Christ himself. The first generations of Sisters have handed the same conviction down to us. What we inherit from Christ is love: love for God, his Father, love for each other and love for all people, especially the poor who are abandoned by the world.
From the beginning until today, the life of every Sister of Charity has been, and remains, a reality of grace which finds expression in:
An apostolic service which stems from our union with God and itself nourishes this same union;
Prayer, which is waiting on the Lord, who himself opens us to his presence and enables us to collaborate in his work;
Community life, which intensifies our apostolic dynamism and is an effective sign of our communion with Him.
Fr. Triest directed us especially to the care of the poor, sick and afflicted and to the education of children and young people. Pauperes evangelizantur. In order to restore man to his human dignity and to help young and old in their manifold needs, we commit ourselves, today as yesterday, to undertake all kinds of work of charity according to the spirit of St. Vincent de Paul. This mission, accomplished with discerning charity, knows no geographical or cultural boundaries. Beati misericordes.

The Society of St. Vincent de Paul (SVP) charity is a Christian voluntary organisation, working with poor and disadvantaged people. Inspired by our principal founder, Frederic Ozanam, and our patron, St. Vincent de Paul, we seek to respond to the call every Christian receives to bring the love of Christ to those in need: 'I was hungry and you gave me food' (Matthew 25). No work of charity is foreign to the Society. We are involved in a diverse range of activities characterised by:-  
  #  Support and friendship: 
Through person-to-person contact, we are committed to respecting the dignity of those we assist and fostering self-respect. We assure confidentiality at all times and endeavour to establish relationships based on trust and friendship.
  #  Promoting self-sufficiency: 
It is not enough to provide short term material support. Those we assist are also helped to achieve self-sufficiency in the longer term and the sense of self-worth this provides. When problems are beyond our competence, we enlist the support of specialised help.
  #  Working for Social Justice: 
We are committed to identifying the root causes of poverty and social exclusion in Ireland and, in solidarity with poor and disadvantaged people, to advocate and work for the changes required to create a more just and caring society.

name: Trocaire
address: Maynooth, Co Kildare, , , Kildare, Republic of Ireland
charitable_purpose: Relief of poverty or economic hardship
charitable_objects:
2.1 Trócaire shall have the following purposes:
2.1.1	The relief of poverty,
2.1.2	The advancement of education, and
2.1.3	Such further or other purpose other than 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 above as the same shall be exclusively charitable.
2.2	Without in any way restricting the generality of the foregoing the Trustees shall endeavour to further the objects of Trócaire by the following methods insofar as the same shall be exclusively charitable in their purposes:- 
Inspired by Christian faith and informed by Catholic social teaching by striving in its structures and organisation to promote the following values:
Respect for human dignity;
Freedom of people from injustice and poverty;
Active promotion of equity and equality among people, addressing specifically the issues of race and gender based inequalities;
Participation of all in the work of justice and development; and 
Justice as the basis for all our actions.
Working with other Church commissions, Christian churches and development organisations in Ireland and with like minded organisations throughout the world.
2.2.1	By establishing an organisation through which:
2.2.1.1 	The Irish Catholic community can express its commitment and response to the needs and problems of developing communities and the principles of social justice involved by contributing funds to further these objectives.
2.2.1.2 	Whatever help lies within the resources of Trócaire is given to the areas of greatest need among the developing countries.
2.2.1.3 	An awareness is created among the Catholic community in Ireland, through an on-going educational and communication process, of the needs and problems of under-developed communities, of the principles of social justice and of the causes of injustice and underdevelopment.
2.2.1.4 	Work can be carried out in partnership and solidarity with the peoples of the developing world to overcome poverty and injustice regardless of creed, race or gender through supporting development projects which are in the main conceived and implemented by the peoples of the developing world and in which such people's participation is the main driving force.
2.2.1.5 	It is recognised that the causes of world poverty lie primarily in unjust social, political and economic structures and national and international structures which maintain the unjust world order are challenges through advocacy and education.
2.2.1.6 	The Fund will be administered so as to ensure that there will be full accountability to the donors and the public at large for the funds donated to Trócaire.

The principal objective of the Charity is to carry out charitable works connected with the Congregation of the Mission and for the advancement of the Roman Catholic Religion.
The Congregation of the Mission was established by a French priest, later saint, of the Catholic Church, St. Vincent de Paul, and members commit to continuing to live out the charism which St. Vincent de Paul lived by and which he sought to imbue in those who shared his vision for the good of humanity.  Central to this charism is the service of people who are poor and whose basic needs St. Vincent de Paul witnessed to be neglected in the society in which he lived.  The motto of the Congregation he founded is based on the vocation of Jesus Christ Himself who declared that He had come to bring Good News to the Poor (Luke 4: 18).
St. Vincent de Paul founded the Congregation to serve the poor primarily by helping them to come to understand the transforming power of Gods grace in their lives.  Members of the Congregation seek to promote this objective by their respectful service of poor people in helping them to become agents of their own transformation.  The twin means used to promote this objective are missions which reach out to those in need and formation.
